items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: to replace Stan Getz who had some court thing he had to appear at

ctx.x: That’s right. Some sophisticated changes that were demanding, yeah challenging is the word, that’s right. So that was fun. And a few things like that through the years don’t have a lot of record solo space. The first solo I played on a record was on a Billy May record called “Bacchanalia” and that was in 1953 I think. That was the first solo I played on a record. And then Ken Hanna was sort of in that period of time. And then Bethlehem hired me to do an album of my own in 1955 and that’s when they were still…

just hanging out or whatever. And the phone would ring and you’d say, “Oh maybe it’s Benny Goodman.” Well one time it was. And he complimented me on that album. He had heard it in New York. And he subsequently hired me to sub on the movie “The Benny Goodman Story” when they were making that movie, to replace Stan Getz. I didn’t have to solo, but to replace Stan Getz who had some court thing he had to appear at, or I don’t know what the details were. So I met him. And then around the same time I got a call from…
